Cash generated from operating activities in the year ended December 31, 2024 was $1,955 million and included Net income from continuing operations of $2,050 million, non-cash charges primarily for depreciation and amortization of $580 million, and $675 million in outflows from incremental changes in assets and liabilities, primarily driven by company-funded benefit payments for postretirement benefit plans, an increase in receivables due to higher volume, and a build in inventories.

Cash generated from operating activities in the year ended December 31, 2023 was $2,101 million and included Net income from continuing operations of $1,618 million, non-cash charges primarily for depreciation and amortization of $610 million, and $127 million in outflows from incremental changes in assets and liabilities, primarily driven by company-funded benefit payments for postretirement benefit plans and an increase in receivables, partially offset by lower cash taxes paid and a decrease in inventories.

Cash generated from operating activities in the year ended December 31, 2022 was $2,134 million and included Net income from continuing operations of $1,949 million, non-cash charges for depreciation and amortization of $633 million, and a $448 million outflow from changes in assets and liabilities, primarily driven by an increase in both inventories and receivables, and higher cash taxes pai.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: Cash used for capital expenditures was $401 million, $387 million, and $310 million for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively. Capital expenditures were primarily for manufacturing capacity expansion, new product introductions, and equipment and tooling for new and existing products.

fcf.heading: Free cash flow*
fcf.text:
Free cash flow* was $1,554 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 and primarily included $1,955 million of cash generated from operating activities, partially offset by $401 million of cash used for additions to PP&E.

Free cash flow* was $1,715 million for the year ended December 31, 2023 and primarily included $2,101 million of cash generated from operating activities, partially offset by $387 million of cash used for additions to PP&E.

Free cash flow* was $1,828 million for the year ended December 31, 2022 and primarily included $2,134 million of cash generated from operating activities, partially offset by $310 million of cash used for additions to PP&E.

gp.text: • Gross profit increased $43 million, but decreased 170 basis points as a percent of Total revenues primarily due to an increase in both Cost of products and Cost of services as a percent of Total revenues. Cost of products sold increased $671 million or 220 basis points as a percent of Sales of products. The increase as a percent of sales was driven by cost inflation, including the impact of incremental tariffs, and investment in design follow-through, partially offset by cost productivity. Cost of services sold increased $240 million or 90 basis points as a percent of Sales of services. The increase as a percent of sales was driven by unfavorable mix within our service offerings, and cost inflation, including the impact of incremental tariffs, partially offset by an increase in pricing of our service offerings. Included in our total cost of revenues as part of our product investment was $490 million in engineering costs for design follow-through on new product introductions and product lifecycle maintenance subsequent to the initial product launch, compared to $405 million for the prior year comparable period ; and

fcf.text: We report Free cash flow to provide management and investors with an important measure of our ability to generate cash on a normalized basis and provide insight into our flexibility to allocate capital. Free cash flow is Cash from (used for) operating activities – continuing operations including cash flows related to the additions and dispositions of property, plant, and equipment (“PP&E”) and additions of internal-use software. Free cash flow does not represent residual cash flows available for discretionary expenditures, due to the fact that the measure does not deduct the capital required for debt repayments.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Our ability to market and sell our products globally depends upon our compliance with the laws and regulations in each jurisdiction in which we develop, manufacture, or distribute our products.

We rely on the timely supply of components, products, services, and solutions from suppliers.
Further, we have multiple single-source or sole-source suppliers with no alternatives yet identified.
Our dependence on such single- or sole-source suppliers subjects us to the risk of possible shortages, interruptions, and price fluctuations.

Disruptions or loss of any of our single- or sole-source suppliers, or capacity limitations of these suppliers, could increase our costs, curtail growth opportunities, cause material delays, and adversely impact our business, financial results, and customer relationships.
We rely upon supplies of certain raw materials, including helium, iodine, and rare earth minerals.
For example, we rely on contract manufacturing organizations to produce certain of our molecular imaging pharmaceutical products.

We rely on third-party transport and warehouse management services for reliable and secure point-to-point transportation of our products to our customers and patients, tracking of these shipments, and warehousing of our products.
We rely on software, SaaS, hardware, and other material components from a number of third parties to manufacture our products or otherwise operate our business.
We also rely on agreements with certain employees, consultants and other parties to protect, in part, trade secrets and other proprietary rights.

In addition, the opinions and the private letter ruling rely on certain facts, assumptions, representations, and undertakings from GE and us regarding the past and future conduct of the companies’ respective businesses and other matters.

We believe that our performance and future success depend on a number of factors that present significant opportunities for us but also pose risks and challenges, including those discussed below and particularly in Item 1A, “Risk Factors.”
